subject: ventures/atm-route-margin
professional: an independent ATM operator / ISO running a route of merchant-placed machines; first checks: is the location split taken on surcharge, is processing per transaction including non-withdrawal transactions, is interchange income counted, is vault cash carry on the average balance, are armored/cash-loading and machine/telecom/compliance costs per visit or per month, and does a route of 20-60 machines roll up

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs on three hand-computed locations (`node /tmp/claude-0/audit-atm/run.mjs`). Defaults: 220x2.75=605; 40% split 242; processing 66; 3000x8%/12=20; mileage 10x0.67x4=26.80; labor 160 min=2.667 h x 25=66.67; machine 60; net 123.53: match. Case B (450 wd, $3.50, 25% + $50 flat, $0.18 proc, 9% on $8,000, 6 visits of 20+30 min, 14 mi at $0.70, $30/h, $95 machine): 1575 - (443.75+81+60+58.80+150+95) = 686.45: match. Case C armored-serviced (1,200 wd, $3, 50%, $0.25, 7.5% on $20,000, 8 armored visits at $85, $120 machine): 3600 - 3025 = 575: match. Route roll-up 124+58 = 182, gap to 1,200 = 1,018, ceil(1018/91) = 12: match. Not a 3: (1) the headline line under the profit, 'about $46.33/hr after all costs' on the defaults, is netProfit/laborHours where netProfit has already paid the operator $25/h for those same hours; what the operator actually earns per hour is (123.53+66.67)/2.667 = $71.33 (case B: shows $137.29, true $167.29), so the displayed rate is understated by exactly the target rate; (2) on the page a blank field, or '1,200' typed in a type=number input (HTML value sanitization returns ''), becomes Number('')=0 with no error: a blank surcharge shows a -$239.47 location instead of a prompt; a blank target income becomes 0 via `|| 0` and the route shows 'Goal met'.
evidence.completeness: Features checked by running or reading the shipped page: per-location profit with commission % and/or flat fee (works), processor per-txn fee (works), vault cash cost (works), labor/mileage/armored (works), machine cost (works), route roll-up and income gap with additional-locations count (works), local draft save, reset and shareable link (share.test.mjs passes, index.html:119-233 read), usage opt-out with DNT/GPC (usage.mjs read, tests pass), four SEO/guide pages present and linked from the sitemap (page.test.mjs). Live page https://marisstella.app/atm-route-margin/ returned 200 with canonical on marisstella.app; served llms.txt origins only marisstella.app and github.com. Limits: the route table is fixed at six rows (index.html:71-76) and each location must be priced above and its profit retyped by hand; no stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/atm-route-margin && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 82 tests, 82 pass, 195 ms. Four seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: armored cost not multiplied by visits SURVIVED (every test uses armoredCostPerVisit 0); effective hourly rate changed to (netProfit+laborCost)/laborHours SURVIVED (no test asserts effectiveHourlyRate at all); Math.ceil -> Math.round in incomeGap caught; labor minutes not multiplied by visits caught. Tests are hand-computed for the default case, but the two derived outputs a user reads first after profit (hourly rate, armored line) are unguarded, and no test covers blank or comma input through the page.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (166 lines), calc.test.mjs, index.html script (index.html:103-235), share.mjs, usage.mjs. Pure functions, one DEFAULTS source shared with share.mjs and the page, textContent-only DOM writes, guarded storage, stale results hidden on error. Defects: number() accepts '' as 0 because Number('') === 0 (calc.mjs:51), so the validation the page relies on never sees a blank; `parseFloat(...) || 0` silently zeroes a blank target (index.html:171); a route row with a genuine $0 profit is dropped from the count and the average (index.html:167).
evidence.claims: Checked: disclaimer (no-warranty + not-advice) on index.html footer, README and guide pages: present. Privacy 'nothing uploaded': backed (no fetch in any script). Guide worked example matches calc.mjs (page.test.mjs:136 passes). Not backed: (a) 'about $X/hr after all costs' (index.html:144) is not the operator's hourly earnings, see correctness; (b) vs-atm-depot.html:79 and :87 and README.md:22 say nothing is 'saved when you close the tab', while index.html:92 and the code save visit inputs to localStorage; (c) README.md:22 lists two counted events, the page four, and the code records a fifth, sponsor_link_clicked (index.html:189), which the page's privacy line does not name; (d) vs-atm-depot.html:85 'prices every location on your own route' with a six-row table and no per-location inputs in the route.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: price a bar placement doing 220 withdrawals, then roll up a route. One location works in under a minute. A real independent route (20-60 machines) cannot be entered in a six-row table, and nothing ties a priced location to a row, so the operator retypes each profit. The ISO's revenue side is incomplete: no interchange income per withdrawal (the processor fee field rejects a negative, so a net rebate cannot be entered: `processingFeePerTxn: -0.15` -> error), and no count of non-withdrawal transactions (balance inquiries, denials) that the processor bills but earn no surcharge. Compliance and fixed costs (EMV/ADA upgrades, PCI, insurance, cash shortage) must be folded into machine cost by hand; the result panel says so.
evidence.domain: Compared against how an ISO route is costed in practice (processor settlement statements: per-approved-withdrawal surcharge and interchange credits, per-transaction processing debits on all transactions; vault cash providers bill a rate on the average daily balance; armored carriers bill per stop). Matches: split on gross surcharge, flat placement fee, per-txn processing, carry on average balance, armored per visit. Departs: no interchange line, no inquiry/denial transactions, mileage default $0.67 is the 2024 IRS rate (IRS 2025 standard rate is 70 cents, IR-2024-312), and the hourly-rate output conflates profit after a wage with earnings per hour.

verdict: Below the bar. The per-location arithmetic is right: three hand-computed locations (self-serviced, mixed split plus flat fee, armored-serviced) and the route gap all match, the page ships at marisstella.app with the disclaimer and an opt-out local counter, and 82 tests pass. But the line an operator reads right after the profit, 'about $46.33/hr after all costs', is understated by the $25 wage the profit already paid (true $71.33), and nothing tests it; blank or comma-typed fields silently become zero; and the ISO revenue model has no interchange line and no non-withdrawal transactions, while the route table stops at six rows. Correctness, claims and verification are each 2, so the bar fails on all three gates.
